from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Determinants calculate the signed area of a parallelogram.",
            "In 2D, these vectors span a simple flat plane.",
            "This area is defined by the formula ad minus bc."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Vectors and Determinants", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        v_a = Vector([1, 2], color="#FF5733")
        v_b = Vector([2, 0.5], color="#33FF57")
        origin = ORIGIN
        
        # Parallelgram area
        parallelogram = Polygon(origin, v_a.get_end(), v_a.get_end() + v_b.get_end(), v_b.get_end(), color="#33A1FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        formula = MathTex(r"|A, B| = a_x b_y - a_y b_x", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.place_at_grid(v_a, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(v_b, 'B4')
        self.play(Create(v_a), Create(v_b))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'E2', 'F5')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Cross Product: Direction and Magnitude", 
                          ["The cross product creates a new 3D vector.", 
                           "Its length equals the parallelogram's area.", 
                           "Direction follows the right-hand rule."])
        
        # Setup 3D elements
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Create vectors
        vec_a = Arrow(ORIGIN, [1, 0.5, 0], buff=0, color=BLUE)
        vec_b = Arrow(ORIGIN, [0, 1, 0.5], buff=0, color=GREEN)
        vec_p = Arrow(ORIGIN, [0, 0, 1.5], buff=0, color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Create(vec_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Parallelogram visual
        para = Polygon(ORIGIN, [1, 0.5, 0], [1, 1.5, 0.5], [0, 1, 0.5], color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(para))
        self.play(Create(vec_p))
        label_p = MathTex(r"\vec{A} \times \vec{B}", color=YELLOW).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_p, "B4")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Intuition: The Parallelogram Expansion", [
            "Varying vectors change the parallelogram's shape.",
            "The cross product length scales with this area.",
            "Wider angles create longer perpendicular vectors."
        ])
        
        # Setup vectors for animation
        vec_a = Vector(LEFT*1.5 + UP*0.5, color=BLUE)
        vec_b = Vector(RIGHT*1.5 + UP*0.2, color=GREEN)
        parallelogram = Polygon(ORIGIN, vec_a.get_end(), vec_a.get_end()+vec_b.get_end(), vec_b.get_end(), 
                                fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_color=WHITE)
        
        group = VGroup(vec_a, vec_b, parallelogram)
        self.place_in_area(group, "A2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Cross product vector
        cp_vec = Vector(OUT, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(cp_vec, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(group), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF33A1"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(GrowArrow(cp_vec), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(vec_b.animate.rotate(0.5, about_point=ORIGIN), 
                  parallelogram.animate.rotate(0.5, about_point=ORIGIN),
                  cp_vec.animate.set_length(2.0),
                  self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33A1FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The cross product tracks spatial orientation.",
            "It acts like an exterior algebra wedge product.",
            "Transformations distort the volume's spanned area."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Transformations and the Cross Product", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2]).scale(0.5)
        basis = VGroup(
            Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color=RED),
            Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color=GREEN),
            Arrow(ORIGIN, OUT, color=BLUE)
        )
        transformed_basis = VGroup(
            Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT + UP, color=RED),
            Arrow(ORIGIN, UP + OUT, color=GREEN),
            Arrow(ORIGIN, OUT + RIGHT, color=BLUE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(basis))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        wedge_text = Text("Wedge Product", font_size=20, color="#5733FF")
        self.place_at_grid(wedge_text, 'A3')
        self.play(Write(wedge_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Transform(basis, transformed_basis))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Cross products find normals in computer graphics.",
            "They calculate physical moments in mechanics.",
            "They define orientations within linear algebra."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: Why It Matters", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colored mobjects
        obj1 = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE),
            Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=YELLOW)
        )
        obj2 = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*1, RIGHT*1, color=GREEN),
            Dot(color=RED, radius=0.15)
        )
        obj3 = VGroup(
            Axes(x_range=[-1, 1], y_range=[-1, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(obj1, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(obj1), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(obj2, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(obj2), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(obj3, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(obj3), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometric Essence of Cross Products: From Areas to Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors and Determinants
sections.content: Briefly recall that a 2D determinant represents the signed area of a parallelogram spanned by two vectors. Connect this 2D 'area' concept to the 3D 'cross product' concept.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2x2 grid where the area shaded by vectors (a, b) and (c, d) is defined by ad-bc.

sections.title: Defining the Cross Product: Direction and Magnitude
sections.content: Explain that the cross product of two 3D vectors results in a third vector. Magnitude = Area of the parallelogram spanned by the two vectors; Direction = Right-hand rule (perpendicular to the plane).
sections.example: Using a robotic arm with two joints; the cross product represents the 'normal force' or axis of rotation required to move the arm.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: The Parallelogram Expansion
sections.content: Visualize how moving one vector while keeping the other fixed changes the resultant cross product vector's length, representing the changing surface area of the parallelogram.
sections.example: Animation of a 'stretching' rubber sheet spanning two vectors: as the angle widens, the cross product vector grows in length.

sections.title: Linear Transformations and the Cross Product
sections.content: Connect the cross product to the concept of the 'wedge product' in exterior algebra. Explain that the cross product tracks how a linear transformation affects the 3D volume/orientation.
sections.example: A 3D character (e.g., a cartoon cube) undergoing a transformation; tracking the cross product of its edge vectors reveals how the shape is tilted and stretched.

sections.title: Summary: Why It Matters
sections.content: Summarize that the cross product isn't just a formula; it's a tool to find normals in graphics, moments in physics, and volume orientations in linear algebra.
sections.example: Lighting calculation in a video game: calculating the normal of a surface using the cross product to determine how shadows fall on a 3D character.
